subject: adult-health-medicine
title: Thyroid disorders: high-yield principles for NEET-PG, INI-CET and FMGE

steps.tx: Thyrotoxicosis means excess circulating thyroid hormone, whatever the cause. Common causes include **Graves disease**, toxic nodules, and **thyroiditis**. Graves disease is an autoimmune disorder in which **TSH receptor antibodies** stimulate the gland. Clinically, look for a diffuse non-tender goitre, eye signs and a high heart rate. Biochemistry is typically a suppressed TSH with raised free T4.

steps.tx: Distinguish causes by the **radioiodine uptake** scan. Graves disease and toxic nodules show high uptake, with focal uptake in a hyperfunctioning nodule in the latter. **Painful thyroiditis** and amiodarone-induced destructive thyroiditis show low uptake, because preformed hormone is released rather than newly made. Thyrotoxicosis with a low uptake is therefore not treated with antithyroid drugs.

steps.tx: Start an **antithyroid drug** such as **carbimazole**, which the body converts to **methimazole**. This blocks **thyroid peroxidase**, so iodine cannot be built into hormone, and synthesis falls over several weeks. Add a **beta blocker** such as propranolol for fast relief of palpitations and tremor, as its effect begins within hours. Carbimazole is the usual first choice in India.

steps.tx: **Thyroid storm** is a rare but **life-threatening** decompensation of hyperthyroidism, marked by fever, fast heart rate, agitation and vomiting. Start treatment on clinical suspicion rather than waiting for laboratory confirmation. Block new hormone synthesis first with a **thionamide**, then give iodine so it does not feed fresh hormone production. Add a **beta blocker** to control adrenergic symptoms, and consider corticosteroids to reduce conversion of T4 to T3. Ask about recent omission of antithyroid tablets.
steps.say: Thyroid storm is a rare but life-threatening flare of hyperthyroidism. It shows up as fever, a fast heart rate, agitation and vomiting. Start treatment on clinical suspicion rather than waiting for lab confirmation. Give a thionamide first to block new hormone synthesis, then iodine, so it does not feed fresh hormone production. Add a beta blocker to control adrenergic symptoms, and consider corticosteroids to reduce conversion of T4 to T3. Always ask whether the patient has recently stopped their antithyroid tablets, because that is a common trigger.

steps.tx: Thyroid nodules need assessment for malignancy. A **firm solitary nodule** with normal TSH and suspicious ultrasound features, such as an irregular margin or **microcalcification**, warrants **ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration** for cytology. Scintigraphy is used when TSH is suppressed, to check whether a nodule is autonomous. Imaging with contrast CT is not the first-line test for thyroid nodule assessment.
